organism.strainConstruction: hipA7 from HM22 transduced into MGY, an MG1655-derived constitutive-YFP background; selected clone sequence-verified by Balaban et al.

primarySource.citation: Balaban et al. (2004), Bacterial Persistence as a Phenotypic Switch

sourceContext.supportingMaterial: Balaban et al. 2004 Supplementary Online Material
sourceContext.microfluidicGrowth: Aerated LBL continuously flowed; hipA7 experiments started from overnight cultures.
sourceContext.batchSurvivalAssay: Cultures or aliquots were exposed to 100 ug/mL ampicillin and viable survivors were enumerated by plating after treatment.

states.label: type-I persister / growth-arrested
states.inheritance: phenotypic, reversible; survivors regrow as antibiotic-sensitive progeny

normalToPersister.limitation: Balaban et al. explicitly limit the a≈0 approximation to high-persistence hipA7 experiments after passage through stationary phase, where smaller persister subpopulations could be occluded. This is not a universal zero switching rate.

stationaryPhaseEntry.authority: Type-I persisters are generated during/after stationary phase, but the source does not provide a portable continuous N→Q rate or a Petra-resource threshold law.
stationaryPhaseEntry.implementationRule: Do not synthesize an endogenous stationary-phase switching rate. A scenario must either initialize a source-calibrated Q fraction or add a separately validated trigger law.

persisterToNormal.sourceObservation: A long-lag hipA7 subpopulation had an approximately 14 h exit-from-stationary-phase time scale; Balaban et al. identify its inverse as b≈0.07 h^-1.
persisterToNormal.limitation: This recovery rate is specific to the source fresh-LBL exit assay and is not a universal wake-up rate across media or stresses.

growthBehavior.authority: hipA7 type-I persisters were growth-arrested before ampicillin and modeled with mu_p≈0.
growthBehavior.limitation: The pack does not bind an absolute normal-cell growth rate for Petra. Normal growth must come from a compatible source-owned ecology context.

derivedEffectiveExponentialRateScalesPer.derivation: reciprocal of the reported characteristic time
derivedEffectiveExponentialRateScalesPer.warning: These are effective exponential time-scale reciprocals, not independently measured raw mu_n/mu_p parameters. A coupled implementation must reproduce source survival behavior before promoting them as internal hazards.

ampicillinResponse.limitation: Authority is for 100 ug/mL ampicillin in the named LBL context. No concentration-response curve, MIC-shift policy, other-antibiotic response, clinical dose, or spatial transport law is supplied.

reversibilityValidation.target: Progeny recovered from hipA7 persisters become susceptible again on a subsequent ampicillin challenge.
reversibilityValidation.authority: Balaban et al. supplementary Fig. S1 / movie observations.
reversibilityValidation.implementationRule: Persistence state must not mutate MIC or resistance genotype. Q→N recovery restores the ordinary susceptible phenotype unless an independent genetic mutation event has occurred.

supported: two phenotype compartments within one hipA7 genotype
growth-arrested Q state in the source context
fresh-LBL Q→N recovery at b≈0.07 h^-1
source-history dependence: overnight versus exponential inoculum
reversible tolerance distinct from genetic resistance
unbound: single exact stationary-phase initial Q fraction
mapping Petra dimensionless resource to the Balaban stationary-phase trigger
absolute normal-cell growth rate for Petra
ampicillin physical transport or delivery geometry
runtimeAdmission.blocker: A source-compatible stationary-phase entry/initialization calibration and an implementation that passes the survival/reversibility targets are required before exposing this as a quantitative selectable scenario.

provenance.context: Balaban et al. hipA7 MGYA7, LB Lennox, 37 C, 100 ug/mL ampicillin; type-I persistence after stationary-phase history.
provenance.limitation: This record deliberately preserves the source's unresolved stationary-phase entry law. It must not be generalized into a universal E. coli persister fraction or switching rate.
